explanation.text:
On Neginoth, that is, stringed instruments, as the kind of musical accompaniment. On other parts of title, see Introduction., The historical occasion was probably the same as that of the foregoing [see on Psa 3:1]. The writer, praying for further relief, admonishes his enemies of the vanity of attacking God's servant, exhorts them to repentance, and avows his confidence and peace in God's favor. (Psa 4:1-8)

Hear--as in Psa 3:4.

God of my righteousness--or, "my righteous God, as my holy hill" (Psa 2:6), who will act towards me on righteous principles.

thou hast enlarged--expresses relief afforded in opposition to "distress," which is expressed by a word denoting straits or pressure. Past favor is a ground of hope for the future.

bsb.title: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm of David.
bsb.text: Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! You have relieved my distress; show me grace and hear my prayer.

explanation.text:
sons of men--men of note or prominence (compare Ch2 21:9).

turn my glory--or, "royal dignity."

into shame--or, "reproach."

vanity--a foolish and hopeless enterprise (Psa 2:1).

leasing--a lie.

bsb.text: How long, O men, will my honor be maligned? How long will you love vanity and seek after lies? Selah

explanation.text: godly--an object as well as subject of divine favor (compare Psa 105:14-15).

bsb.text: Know that the LORD has set apart the godly for Himself; the LORD hears when I call to Him.

explanation.text: Stand in awe-- (Eph 4:26), from Septuagint, "be angry." Both clauses are qualified by "not."

bsb.text: Be angry, yet do not sin; on your bed, search your heart and be still. Selah

explanation.text: Not only repent, but manifest penitence by sacrifices or righteousness or righteous sacrifices, etc.

bsb.text: Offer the sacrifices of the righteous and trust in the LORD.

explanation.text:
Contrast true with vain confidence.

light of thy countenance upon us--figure for favor (Num 6:26; Psa 44:3; Psa 81:16).

bsb.text: Many ask, “Who can show us the good?” Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD.

explanation.text:
corn and wine--literally, "new corn and wine."

increased--an abundant harvest giving great joy (Isa 9:3).

bsb.text: You have filled my heart with more joy than when grain and new wine abound.

explanation.text:
both lay me down, etc.--or, will lie down at once, and sleep in sure confidence and quiet repose (Psa 3:5).

Next: Psalms Chapter 5

bsb.text: I will lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety.
